name: Dispensary Districts 1 Apr 1924
description: The 177 dispensary districts of Northern Ireland from 1 Apr 1924, when Portaferry dispensary district moved from Downpatrick to Newtownards Union, until 31 Dec 1928; this is the state recorded by the census of 18 Apr 1926. Each district is a group of the old (pre-1923) electoral divisions on Civgraph's 3 May 1921 DED map (Paddy Matthews, with Phelim Birch's corrections), because the Ministry of Home Affairs ordered in 1925 that dispensary districts stay as they were before the 1923 reconstitution of the divisions. The district of each old division is the one its townlands carry in the 1926 Census Topographical Index, checked against the district lists of the 1926 county volumes (Table 4) and the order of the 1911 Census Table VI. Ten old divisions were shared between districts; these are split on OSNI townland lines (Brownlows Derry, Ballygomartin, Ballysillan, Monkstown, Ardclinis, Beardiville, Portrush Rural, Kilkeel, Newry Rural and Drumnakilly). The 16 Belfast urban districts and the Londonderry urban districts other than Waterside cross ward lines along streets, so each county borough's urban districts are shown as one undivided area. With the large loughs taken out, 93 of the 97 county parts whose 1926 printed area could be read agree within 2% (median 0.06%); each district carries its grade and the reason for it (confidence, confidence_reason). Dispensary districts were also the registrars' districts for births, deaths and marriages.

references.label: Belfast Gazette issue 105 (Downpatrick and Newtownards Unions)
references.note: 29 Jun 1923, pp. 300, 316-317. Ardkeen, Portaferry and Quintin electoral divisions (Portaferry dispensary district) separated from Downpatrick Union and added to Newtownards Union from 1 Apr 1924.

references.label: Belfast Gazette issue 229 (Poor Law Dispensary Districts)
references.note: 13 Nov 1925, p. 338. Ministry of Home Affairs order under s. 9(1) of the Local Government Act (NI) 1923: the boundaries and contents of the dispensary districts remain as they were before the orders altering the district electoral divisions.

references.label: Census of Population of Northern Ireland 1926: Topographical Index
references.note: Index 6 (dispensary or registrars' districts, with their union) and Index 9 (townlands, each with its dispensary district), read from the OCR text; about 6,200 townland entries matched to OSNI townlands.

references.note: Poor Law Unions, Dispensary Districts and District Electoral Divisions: the DEDs (and parts of DEDs) in each dispensary district, with its area; used to check placements and areas.

references.label: Census of Population of Northern Ireland 1926: General Report
references.note: p. xvii: 178 medical dispensary districts in Northern Ireland (177 at the census date, the Topographical Index introduction says).
